'''''007 Legends''''' is a 2012 [[first-person shooter game]] featuring the fictional British secret agent [[James Bond (Daniel Craig)|James Bond]]. It was developed by [[Eurocom]] and published by [[Activision]] in October 2012 for [[PlayStation 3]] and [[Xbox 360]], with [[Microsoft Windows]] and [[Wii U]] versions being released later that year. The Wii U release of the game was cancelled in Australia and the game was removed from all digital storefronts in January 2013.

The game was released to coincide with the fiftieth anniversary of the [[James Bond in film|James Bond film series]]. To achieve this, the single player campaign includes one mission from each of the six actors' eras: ''[[Goldfinger (film)|Goldfinger]]'' ([[Sean Connery]]), ''[[On Her Majesty's Secret Service (film)|On Her Majesty's Secret Service]]'' ([[George Lazenby]]), ''[[Moonraker (film)|Moonraker]]'' ([[Roger Moore]]), ''[[Licence to Kill]]'' ([[Timothy Dalton]]) and ''[[Die Another Day]]'' ([[Pierce Brosnan]]). A level based on ''[[Skyfall]]'' ([[Daniel Craig]]) was later released as free downloadable content for the Xbox 360, PlayStation 3 and Microsoft Windows versions, and included on disc on the Wii U version. Additionally, some of the original talent from the films add their likenesses and voices to their associated characters.

Upon its release, ''007 Legends'' received generally negative reviews from critics, who criticized the choice of missions, bland gameplay, and lack of an overarching story, though its multiplayer mode did attract some praise. It is the fourth and final James Bond game released by Activision and the last game Eurocom developed before the company ceased operations. There were no further major ''James Bond'' games made until ''[[007 First Light]]'' in 2026.

==Gameplay==
[[File:007 legends gameplay.png|thumb|right|''007 Legends'' is a [[first-person shooter]] game that serves as a retelling of key moments in the [[James Bond]] franchise. Here the player navigates through a level based on the film ''[[Moonraker (film)|Moonraker]]''.]]
''007 Legends'' is a [[first-person shooter]] game in which the player controls [[James Bond (Daniel Craig)|James Bond]] in [[level (video games)|levels]] based on the films ''[[Die Another Day]]'', ''[[Goldfinger (film)|Goldfinger]]'', ''[[Licence to Kill]]'', ''[[Moonraker (film)|Moonraker]]'', and ''[[On Her Majesty's Secret Service (film)|On Her Majesty's Secret Service]]''.<ref name="Polygon Review">{{cite web|last=McElroy|first=Justin|url=https://www.polygon.com/2012/10/25/3551080/007-legends-review/|title=007 Legends review: die today|website=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]]|date=25 October 2012|accessdate=25 August 2025}}</ref>{{efn-ua|An additional level, based on the film ''[[Skyfall]]'', was later added as [[downloadable content]].<ref name="DLC Level">{{cite web|last=Goldfarb|first=Andrew|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2012/10/20/007-legends-skyfall-dlc-coming-next-month|title=007 Legends Skyfall DLC Coming Next Month|website=[[IGN]]|date=19 October 2012|accessdate=25 August 2025}}</ref>}} The gameplay largely consists of firefights against groups of enemies across multiple locations, which several critics compared to the gameplay of the ''[[Call of Duty]]'' franchise.<ref name="Polygon Review"/><ref name="IGN Review"/><ref name="Eurogamer Review"/> While in combat, the player can use [[iron sights]], crouch behind cover, and vault over objects.<ref name="Manual"/> Throughout the game, there are occasional sections in which the player will need to sneak past enemies.<ref name="IGN Review"/> During these stealth sections, the player can knock out unsuspecting enemies or kill them with a silenced gun.<ref name="IGN Review"/> The player also has access to gadgets to make the stealth sections easier, such as a wristwatch with radar to detect enemy movement, and tranquilizer darts to subdue enemies from long distance.<ref name="PSBlog">{{cite web|last=Matthews|first=Rob|url=https://blog.playstation.com/2012/10/16/007-legends-celebrates-bond-history-today-ps3-exclusive-multiplayer-characters/|title=007 Legends Celebrates Bond History Today, PS3-Exclusive Multiplayer Characters|website=[[PlayStation Blog]]|date=16 October 2012|accessdate=28 August 2025}}</ref>

Whenever the player completes in-game challenges, such as kill a certain amount of enemies with one gun, they earn [[experience point]]s.<ref name="Polygon Review"/><ref name="Manual"/> These can be used to purchase weapon upgrades and character improvements such as increased health and aiming speed.<ref name="Polygon Review"/><ref>{{cite web|last=Leone|first=Matt|url=https://www.polygon.com/gaming/2012/6/6/3067315/007-legends-is-part-of-the-industrys-disappearing-middle/|title='007 Legends' is part of the industry's disappearing middle|website=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]]|date=6 June 2012|accessdate=28 August 2025}}</ref> In addition to gunfights, there are also melee fights against [[Boss (video games)|bosses]] and driving sections.<ref name="Polygon Review"/> The melee fights feature [[quick time event]]s, in which the player can punch by pressing the corresponding button when prompted.<ref name="Polygon Review"/> In the driving sections, the player escapes from pursuing enemies while dodging projectiles like rockets.<ref name="Polygon Review"/>

''007 Legends'' features shorter single-player levels called MI6-Ops.<ref name="PSBlog"/> These levels revolve around specific challenges, such as stealthily infiltrating a compound without alerting the target, or defending an objective against waves of enemies.<ref name="Manual">{{cite book|title=007 Legends Manual|publisher=[[Eurocom]]|year=2012}}</ref> If the level is completed, the player is given a [[Score (video games)|score]] based on the difficulty option selected and the amount of time it took to complete the level.<ref name="Manual"/> The score for MI6-Ops levels are ranked on online leaderboard against other players.<ref name="Manual"/> ''007 Legends'' also features [[Multiplayer video game|multiplayer]], which can be played either online with 12 players or [[Split screen (video games)|split screen]] with four players.<ref name="Manual"/> There are several multiplayer game modes such as killing other players with the golden gun from ''The Man with the Golden Gun'', or racing to collect data from a downed plane.<ref name="GameSpot Review"/> The player can equip gadgets to enhance their abilities in multiplayer, such as a gadget called the Fast Switch, which reduces the time it takes to switch weapons.<ref name="VG247 Preorder">{{cite web|last=Dunn|first=Jeff|url=https://www.vg247.com/007-legends-pre-order-details-revealed|title=007 Legends pre-order details revealed|website=[[VG247]]|date=10 August 2012|accessdate=28 August 2025}}</ref>

==Plot==
The game begins with the opening chase sequence in ''[[Skyfall]]'', in which MI6 agent James Bond (likeness of [[Daniel Craig]], voice of [[Timothy Watson]]) pursues the mercenary Patrice in Istanbul, only to be accidentally shot and wounded aboard a train by his partner [[Miss Moneypenny|Eve Moneypenny]] ([[Naomie Harris]]). Plunging into the river below, Bond begins to flash back to several of his previous missions that took place in-between ''[[Quantum of Solace (film)|Quantum of Solace]]''  and ''Skyfall''. However, with the release of ''[[Spectre (2015 film)|Spectre]]'', the game has been rendered as non-canon.

In Miami, Bond awakens in a hotel room to find Jill Masterson dead from skin suffocation, coated in gold paint. Days later in Switzerland, Bond infiltrates the facility of [[Auric Goldfinger]] ([[Timothy Watson]], likeness of [[Gert Fröbe]]), the man responsible for Masterson's death. He discovers Goldfinger's plan to irradiate the United States Gold Depository at [[Fort Knox]], Kentucky in  [[Goldfinger (film)|Operation Grand Slam]]. Bond manages to convince Goldfinger's personal pilot, [[Pussy Galore]] (likeness of [[Honor Blackman]], voice of [[Natasha Little]]), to inform the CIA, and he and the United States Army manage to thwart Goldfinger's scheme in the nick of time.

In the [[Swiss Alps]], Bond and his lover [[Contessa Teresa di Vicenzo|Contessa Teresa "Tracy" di Vicenzo]] (likeness of [[Diana Rigg]], voice of [[Nicola Walker]]), daughter of Italian [[Unione Corse]] boss [[Marc-Ange Draco]], escape via skis after an attack by soldiers of [[Ernst Stavro Blofeld]] ([[Glenn Wrage]]), a terrorist mastermind residing in his mountaintop lair, [[Piz Gloria]]. Bond is injured by a helicopter gunship during the gunfire, and Tracy is in turn captured by Blofeld's men. Sometime later, Bond and Draco lead an aerial attack on Piz Gloria in order to rescue Tracy. They succeed. However, on their honeymoon, Bond and Tracy are attacked by Blofeld and the latter is killed.

Bond finds his CIA agent friend [[Felix Leiter]] ([[Demetri Goritsas]]) maimed in his house alongside his dead wife. The man responsible is [[Franz Sanchez]] (likeness of [[Robert Davi]], voice of Rob David), a Mexican drug lord whom Bond and Leiter had unsuccessfully attempted to take down weeks earlier. On a quest for vengeance, Bond and DEA agent [[Pam Bouvier]] ([[Carey Lowell]]) infiltrate Sanchez's facility inside an old [[Otomi people|Otomi]] temple, intent on killing him. A car chase ensues, and Bond kills Sanchez with the lighter given to him by Felix when Bond found him on the floor.

In Iceland, Bond and NSA agent [[Jinx (James Bond)|Giacinta "Jinx" Johnson]] ([[Madalena Alberto]]) arrive at a party held by billionaire philanthropist [[Gustav Graves]] ([[Toby Stephens]]), who is believed to be involved in the theft of military satellite components. Jinx spots Zao (Jason Wong), a rogue [[Korean People's Army]] operative who killed two of Jinx's colleagues, and believes he may be involved. They learn that Graves plans to weaponize ICARUS, a satellite used to reflect sunlight, in order to destroy South Korean forces on the DMZ, opening the way for a North Korean invasion of the South. Bond and Jinx manage to board Graves' plane after a lengthy car chase with their [[Aston Martin DBS V12]], killing Zao in the process. The ensuing firefight causes the plane to head downwards in a tailspin, but Bond manages to kill Graves and escape with Jinx.

In Brazil, Bond and [[Holly Goodhead]] ([[Jane Perry (actress)|Jane Perry]]), a NASA scientist moonlighting as a CIA agent, infiltrate the rocket launch facility of [[Hugo Drax]] ([[Michael Lonsdale]]), a billionaire industrialist who has started his own private space exploration program. They quickly learn that Drax, a twisted [[Social Darwinism|social Darwinist]], intends to wipe out the human race while creating his own new "master race" from personally-selected specimens, spared from the destruction of Earth via biological weapons onboard Drax's personal space station. Bond and Goodhead manage to get on board the station via a shuttlecraft and proceed to destroy it, killing Drax in the process by blowing him out of an airlock.

Back in the present, Bond regains consciousness on the riverbank, injured, but alive. A few days later, he is seen in Shanghai, following Patrice to prevent the assassination of an unknown figure. Bond succeeds, but kicks Patrice off a building to his death before learning of his employer's identity. After finishing his report to M ([[Judi Dench]]) via phone, he is informed by [[Bill Tanner]] ([[Rory Kinnear]]) that another mission awaits him.

==Development==
[[File:Daniel Craig in 2021.jpg|thumb|right|Actor [[Daniel Craig]] provides Bond's likeness in the game, replacing previous actors in their respective stories.]]
''007 Legends'' was developed by [[Eurocom]], who had previously worked on other ''James Bond'' games, such as ''[[The World Is Not Enough (Nintendo 64 video game)|The World Is Not Enough]]'' (2000), ''[[James Bond 007: Nightfire]]'' (2002), and ''[[GoldenEye 007 (2010 video game)|GoldenEye 007]]'' (2010).<ref>{{cite web|last=Plant|first=Gaz|url=https://www.nintendolife.com/news/2013/01/feature_nintendo_and_bond_through_the_ages|title=Feature: Nintendo and Bond Through the Ages|website=[[Nintendo Life]]|date=19 January 2013|accessdate=27 January 2026}}</ref> For the 50th anniversary of the [[James Bond in film|''James Bond'' film franchise]], holding company [[Danjaq]] and video game publisher [[Activision]] contracted Eurocom to make a game that incorporated key moments from the franchise.<ref name="Hollywood Reporter">{{cite web|last=Gaudiosi|first=John|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/general-news/james-bond-screenwriter-bruce-feirstein-378908/|title=James Bond Screenwriter Bruce Feirstein Explores '007 Legends' With Activision Game|website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|date=15 October 2012|accessdate=27 January 2026}}</ref> Six ''James Bond'' films were selected for ''007 Legends'', with each film corresponding to one of the six actors who have played James Bond.<ref name="PSBlog"/> [[Bruce Feirstein]] and Robin Matthews served as the screenwriters for the game.<ref name="Hollywood Reporter"/><ref>{{cite web|last=McAllister|first=Gillen|url=https://www.gamereactor.eu/007-penning-the-legends/|title=007: Penning the Legends|website=[[Gamereactor]]|date=2 August 2012|accessdate=29 January 2026}}</ref>

The game was first released in North America on 16 October 2012 for [[PlayStation 3]] and [[Xbox 360]]. A [[Microsoft Windows]] release followed on 2 November 2012. The [[Wii U]] received the final platform release in December 2012.<ref name="releasedates">Activision (11 October 2012), [http://community.007legends.com/community/bond/legends_007/blog/2012/10/11/007-legends-release-dates/ "007 Legends Release Dates"] {{webarchive|url=https://archive.today/20130101181742/http://community.007legends.com/community/bond/legends_007/blog/2012/10/11/007-legends-release-dates/ |date=1 January 2013 }}, 007legends.com. Retrieved 12 October 2012.</ref> The game is available as physical optical disc media, as well as a digital release download via [[PlayStation Network]] and [[Xbox Live Marketplace]] on date of release, though it was removed off all other digital stores without warning in January 2013.<ref name="VGCcites007digitalgameremoval">{{cite web |first=David |last=Scammell |url=http://www.videogamer.com/xbox360/007_legends/news/james_bond_games_pulled_from_digital_platforms.html |title=James Bond games pulled from digital platforms |publisher=VideoGamer.com |date=4 One has even been cancelled|publisher=Vooks|date=28 November 2012|access-date=3 January 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130912011338/http://www.vooks.net/here-come-the-aussie-wii-u-game-delays-one-has-even-been-cancelled/|archive-date=12 September 2013|url-status=live|df=dmy-all}}</ref> The single player campaign includes one mission from each of the six actors' eras (although [[Daniel Craig]]'s likeness is used for Bond in all of them), being ''[[Goldfinger (film)|Goldfinger]]'' ([[Sean Connery]]), ''[[On Her Majesty's Secret Service (film)|On Her Majesty's Secret Service]]'' ([[George Lazenby]]), ''[[Moonraker (film)|Moonraker]]'' ([[Roger Moore]]), ''[[Licence to Kill]]'' ([[Timothy Dalton]]) and ''[[Die Another Day]]'' ([[Pierce Brosnan]]), with then-recent release ''[[Skyfall]]'' released as downloadable content for the Xbox 360, PS3 and PC and included on disc for the Wii U version.<ref name=goldfinger>Activision (18 September 2012), [http://community.007legends.com/community/bond/legends_007/blog/2012/09/18/goldfinger-revealed-as-fifth-movie-in-007-legends/ "Goldfinger Revealed as Fifth Movie in 007 Legends"] {{webarchive|url=https://archive.today/20130116041304/http://community.007legends.com/community/bond/legends_007/blog/2012/09/18/goldfinger-revealed-as-fifth-movie-in-007-legends/ |date=16 January 2013 }}, 007legends.com. Retrieved 27 September 2012.</ref> It remained the final James Bond video game until November 2020, when it was announced a new Bond game, ''[[007 First Light]]'', had entered development under [[IO Interactive]].<ref name="new bond">{{Cite web |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/hitman-developer-announces-new-bond-game-project-007 |title=Hitman Developer Announces New Bond Game, Project 007 |publisher=[[IGN]] |accessdate=10 February 2022 |date=19 November 2020 |first=Joe |last=Skrebels}}</ref>

''[[Moonraker (film)|Moonraker]]'' was the first mission of the game to be revealed,<ref>{{cite news|title=007 Legends Game Trailer: Moonraker Level |url=http://www.007legends.com/social_media |work=007 Legends Official Site |date=21 May 2012 |access-date=21 May 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120623140442/http://www.007legends.com/social_media |archive-date=23 June 2012 }}</ref> while the second mission is based on the film ''[[On Her Majesty's Secret Service (film)|On Her Majesty's Secret Service]]''.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.mi6-hq.com/sections/007legendsgame/screenshots_mission_2_ohmss.php3?t=&s=&id=03206 |title=007 Legends - Mission 2 Screenshots - On Her Majesty's Secret Service :: 007 Legends Video Game :: James Bond 007 Gaming |publisher=Mi6-hq.com |date=29 June 2012 |access-date=25 August 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160411194714/https://www.mi6-hq.com/sections/007legendsgame/screenshots_mission_2_ohmss.php3?t=&s=&id=03206 |archive-date=11 April 2016 |url-status=live |df=dmy-all }}</ref> ''[[Goldfinger (film)|Goldfinger]]'' is the opening mission of the game, while ''[[Licence to Kill]]'', and ''[[Die Another Day]]'' (the only film starring Brosnan as Bond which did not originally have a tie-in game) also feature in the story.<ref name=achievements>{{cite news|title=007 Legends achievements|url=http://www.xbox360achievements.org/game/007-legends/achievements/|access-date=16 September 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120920071339/http://www.xbox360achievements.org/game/007-legends/achievements|archive-date=20 September 2012|url-status=live|df=dmy-all}}</ref> The only mission that is not on the game disc itself is the "Skyfall" mission, which was released on 20 November 2012 as free downloadable content (DLC), since ''007 Legends'' was released one week before ''Skyfall'' was first released in theaters. The ''Skyfall'' DLC is available for PlayStation 3, PC and the Xbox 360 and is included on the disc on the Wii U. [[Bruce Feirstein]], who wrote [[James Bond in film|three films]] and [[James Bond (games)|four games]] in the ''James Bond'' universe, wrote the screenplay along with Robin Matthews, who works for Eurocom. The composers from a previous release in the series, [[GoldenEye 007 (2010 video game)|''GoldenEye 007'']], returned to do the music score for ''007 Legends''. [[Kevin Kiner]] wrote and composed the soundtrack, while [[David Arnold]] wrote his own instrumental arrangement of [[Goldfinger (Shirley Bassey song)|''Goldfinger'']] for the main title sequence.<ref>{{cite news|title=Main Title Sequence Preview|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=c4YI9ORTVKs|date=4 October 2012|access-date=4 October 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121004200537/http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=c4YI9ORTVKs&gl=US&hl=en|archive-date=4 October 2012|url-status=live|df=dmy-all}}</ref><ref name="talent">Activision (27 July 2012), [http://community.007legends.com/community/bond/legends_007/blog/2012/07/27/007-legends-to-feature-past-and-present-bond-talent/ "007 Legends to Feature Past and Present Bond Talent"] {{webarchive|url=https://archive.today/20130116011203/http://community.007legends.com/community/bond/legends_007/blog/2012/07/27/007-legends-to-feature-past-and-present-bond-talent/ |date=16 January 2013 }}, 007legends.com. Retrieved 27 September 2012.</ref>

Some additional actors from the films reprise their roles in the game, whether through new voice lines or archival audio. Two ''Moonraker'' actors return to their original roles. [[Richard Kiel]] returns as the silent antagonist [[Jaws (James Bond)|Jaws]], while [[Michael Lonsdale]] returns as villain [[Hugo Drax]]. [[Rory Kinnear]] returns in the role of MI6 chief of staff [[Bill Tanner]], who first portrayed the role in ''[[Quantum of Solace]]''. [[Miss Moneypenny|Eve Moneypenny]] is again played by [[Naomie Harris]], who began portraying the character in 2012's ''[[Skyfall]]''. ''[[Die Another Day]]'' antagonist Gustav Graves is again played by [[Toby Stephens]]. Again, ''[[Licence to Kill|License to Kill]]'' actress [[Carey Lowell]] lends her voice to Pam Bouvier. Other characters have their likenesses retained, but their voices are provided by different actors. [[Timothy Watson]] provides the voice of Craig's James Bond, and also voices [[Auric Goldfinger]], the titular villain from the film ''[[Goldfinger (film)|Goldfinger]]''.<ref name="Eurogamer Review" /> Recurring Bond villain [[Ernst Stavro Blofeld]] is voiced by [[Glenn Wrage]].<ref name="VO actors">{{cite web |url=https://www.digitalspy.com/videogames/a395848/007-legends-cast-includes-jaws-drax-actors/ |title='007 Legends' cast revealed |publisher=[[Digital Spy]] |accessdate=10 February 2022 |date=27 June 2022 |first=Scott |last=Nichols}}</ref>

| NLife = 4/10<ref name="Nintendo Life Review">{{cite web|last=Wahlgren|first=Jon|url=https://www.nintendolife.com/reviews/wiiu/james_bond_007_legends|title=James Bond: 007 Legends Review (Wii U)|website=[[Nintendo Life]]|date=17 December 2012|accessdate=6 September 2025}}</ref>
| XPlay = 1.5/5<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.g4tv.com/games/xbox-360/66093/007-legends/review/ |title=007 Legends Review - Xbox 360 |date=November 5, 2012 |first=Alex |last=Rubens |publisher=[[G4tv|G4]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130311120924/http://www.g4tv.com/games/xbox-360/66093/007-legends/review/ |archive-date=March 11, 2013 |access-date=November 27, 2022}}</ref>

''007 Legends'' received generally unfavorable reviews from critics, according to aggregating review website [[Metacritic]].<ref name=MCPS3 /><ref name=MCX360 /><ref name=MCPC /> Reviewers often commented that the game felt like a missed opportunity, and that it played like a ''[[Call of Duty (franchise)|Call of Duty]]'' clone. Some reviewers noted that the game had small moments that engaged the player as Bond, but that generally gameplay was bland and uninspired. Commentary on the game's multiplayer was mixed. While most lambasted the online play, some appreciated the inclusion of split-screen multiplayer.

Tristan Ogilvie of ''[[IGN]]'' accused the game of drowning out the [[James Bond in film|Bond series']] iconic moments by shoehorning them into a cheap and poorly made ''[[Call of Duty]]'' clone, further adding that the gameplay was boring and repetitive and that production had only made a half-hearted attempt to bind the chosen recreation of films together, and that the lack of overarching story offered little incentive to keep playing.<ref name="IGN Review" /> Dan Ryckert of ''[[Game Informer]]'' was similarly critical of the game, describing it as "a mess of a title that's uninspired at best and nearly broken at worst", and while the review applauded the concept of remaking films in video game form, it also attacked the gameplay mechanics as overly-simplistic with the player following on-screen prompts to perform certain actions, which was broken up by "truly awful" stealth gameplay.<ref name="Game Informer review" /> ''[[Eurogamer]]''{{'}}s Will Porter was critical of its by-the-numbers gameplay and stated "every inch of ''007 Legends'' has been covered in a camo-coloured ''Call of Duty'' paint."<ref name="Eurogamer Review" /> Leif Johnson of ''[[GameSpot]]'' felt that it was an "unfulfilling slog".<ref name="gamespot review">{{Cite web |url=https://www.gamespot.com/reviews/007-legends-review/1900-6398807/ |publisher=[[GameSpot]] |title=007 Legends Review |accessdate=10 February 2022 |date=24 October 2012 |first=Leif |last=Johnson}}</ref>

''[[The Globe and Mail]]'' questioned the choice of missions in the game, claiming that fans considered them to be among the worst installments in the Bond film franchise, and that the game threw players into the middle of missions with little explanation or context to them, concluding that the game "feels like a low-budget knockoff of [...] ''Call of Duty''".<ref name="The Globe and Mail review"/> ''[[IT News Africa]]''{{'}}s Frederick Charles Fripp thought that "it could have been a better game if Eurocom focused more on improving the graphics and changing the game dynamic from a fairly linear shooter to something a bit more complex and through-provoking. {{sic}}" He added that "it does become a bit repetitive after a while, especially if the player does not feel challenged".<ref name="IT News Africa review"/> Will Porter of Eurogamer felt that the heart of the films had been lost. In his review he stated "any personality the movies had is erased by the modern Daniel Craig update."<ref name="Eurogamer Review" />

Some praise was given to the game's split-screen multiplayer modes, with ''IGN''{{'}}s Tristan Ogilvie pointing out that localized split-screen was a feature that had been frequently overlooked in first-person shooter games, before adding that there was little to separate the multiplayer of ''007 Legends'' from that of the [[GoldenEye 007 (2010 video game)|''GoldenEye 007'' remake]].<ref name="IGN Review"/> ''GameSpot''{{'}}s Leif Johnson also praised the split-screen multiplayer, but cited that it was more welcome due to a sparse population for online play.<ref name="gamespot review" /> In ''[[Nintendo Life]]''{{'}}s review of the Wii U version, Jon Wahlgren cited that the game's multiplayer was not good enough to entice players away from their favorite online games.<ref name="nintendolife review">{{Cite web |url=https://www.nintendolife.com/reviews/wiiu/james_bond_007_legends |first=Jon |last=Wahlgren |title=James Bond 007: Legends Review |publisher=[[Nintendo Life]] |accessdate=10 February 2022 |date=17 December 2022}}</ref>

Due to the reception and lowering sales of console games, [[Eurocom]] in 4Q/2012 fired 150 people from a total of 200 staff and decided to focus on mobile games.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.gram.pl/news/2012/11/23/tworcy-007-legends-na-bruku-zaloga-eurocomu-uszczuplona-o-75-proc.shtml |title=Twórcy 007 Legends na bruku. Załoga Eurocomu uszczuplona o 75 proc. |first=Patryk |last=Purczyński |date=23 November 2012 |access-date=15 May 2013 |language=pl |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141013091550/http://www.gram.pl/news/2012/11/23/tworcy-007-legends-na-bruku-zaloga-eurocomu-uszczuplona-o-75-proc.shtml |archive-date=13 October 2014 |url-status=live |df=dmy-all }}</ref> On 4 January 2013, Activision and Steam's online stores pulled the PC versions of ''[[Quantum of Solace (video game)|Quantum of Solace]]'', ''[[Blood Stone (video game)|Blood Stone]]'' and ''007 Legends'', initially without explanation or warning, but which was later revealed as Activision choosing to cease their license agreement to the franchise early, which required them to take down the games.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.neogamr.net/news/james-bond-activision-games-removed-from-steam |title=James Bond Activision games removed from Steam |first=John |last=Callaham |date=2 January 2013 |work=NeoGamr |access-date=19 January 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130115205434/http://www.neogamr.net/news/james-bond-activision-games-removed-from-steam |archive-date=15 January 2013 |url-status=dead |df=dmy-all }}</ref>  Similar actions followed shortly on [[Xbox Live]] and [[PlayStation Network]] for the Xbox 360 and PlayStation 3 versions, also affecting ''[[GoldenEye 007 (2010 video game)#GoldenEye 007: Reloaded|GoldenEye 007: Reloaded]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.gamespot.com/news/activisions-james-bond-games-disappear-from-steam-and-xbox-360-6402017 |title=Activision's James Bond games disappear from Steam and Xbox 360 |first=Martin |last=Gaston |date=4 January 2013 |work=[[GameSpot]] |access-date=19 January 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130115203309/http://www.gamespot.com/news/activisions-james-bond-games-disappear-from-steam-and-xbox-360-6402017 |archive-date=15 January 2013 |url-status=live |df=dmy-all }}</ref> ''007 Legends'' was nominated for Outstanding Achievement in Video Game Writing in the [[Writers Guild of America Awards]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.wga.org/wga-awards/nominees-winners.aspx#videogame |title=Writers Guild Awards |work=wga.org |access-date=28 May 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150901174238/http://www.wga.org/wga-awards/nominees-winners.aspx |archive-date=1 September 2015 }}</ref>
